note: Seeds 101 and 303 made no mistakes and only stopped when the 60 s budget ran out (56 and 58). Seed 202 died at 20 on a tap 1 degree from the dot (-179), with the bar exactly on the 180-degree line. The game counted the bar on the +180 side, but the extractor's wrap180 had turned that raw angle into -180, so the v2 seamSplit check saw no split and said 'pop'. The new extractor keeps the raw bar angle, marks a bar on the line as barOnSeam (a tap there is only a last-chance 'edge'), and marks a dot drawn on the line as dotOnSeam. It judges waiting from the pop positions 1 and 2 frames ahead, so a bar crossing the line waits for the dot's side, and a window cut short by the line is tapped at its last sure spot. The frame step is now the median of recent moves, so a single 0- or 2-frame hiccup no longer skews predictions; the rules are unchanged.
instructions:
Pop the Lock. A bar spins around the centre of a ring and a dot sits on the ring. Tap while the bar is on the dot to pop it: the bar then turns the other way and the dot jumps elsewhere on the ring. Tapping while the bar is off the dot, or letting the bar pass the dot, ends the game. Pop as many dots as you can.
One decision is 17 game-ms, usually one animation frame: the bar turns about stepDeg degrees (about 3) in direction dir; occasionally zero or two frames pass.
FIELDS. gapDeg: degrees the bar still has to turn to be centred on the dot (negative = it has just passed the centre). gapNextDeg: gapDeg at the next decision if you wait. barMoving: the bar moved since the last decision. barReversed: the bar just changed direction, which means a dot was just popped. dotMoving: the dot just jumped to a new place. dotPopped: the dot shown is the one that was just popped; the new dot has not appeared yet. popTolDeg (5) is the sure-pop window around the dot centre; edgeTolDeg (about 8) is where the bar only touches the dot's edge.
THE 180-DEGREE LINE (the leftmost point of the ring): the game compares raw angles, so it never counts a hit across this line. seamSplit: the bar and the dot are on opposite sides of the line; a tap then ends the game. barOnSeam: the bar sits exactly on the line, where the game may count it on either side, so a tap there is a gamble. dotOnSeam: the dot sits exactly on the line; it is taken to be on the lower (negative-angle) side, so a tap on it is a gamble too.
A pop position is a bar position within popTolDeg of the dot centre, on the dot's side of the 180-degree line and not on the line.
tapOutcome = what a tap now does: 'pop' = sure pop (the bar is at a pop position, the dot is not on the line, the bar moved normally since the last decision, the dot is settled); 'edge' = a tap may pop or may end the game (the bar only touches the dot's edge, or the bar or the dot sits on the 180-degree line); 'miss' = a tap ends the game; 'uncertain' = do not tap: the bar did not move or just reversed, or the dot just jumped or was just popped, so the effect of the previous tap is not visible yet (an extra tap right after a pop ends the game); 'none' = the game is over.
waitOutcome = what waiting one decision leads to: 'safe' = the bar will still be short of the pop window (or there is no live dot yet); 'closer' = the next position is a pop position nearer the dot centre (and, if the bar is at a pop position now, two frames passing would not carry it onto or across the 180-degree line), or the bar is crossing the 180-degree line and the position after next is a pop position; 'farther' = the next position is a pop position but not nearer the dot centre, so now is the best moment; 'gameOver' = waiting may leave the bar with no pop position (past the dot, or on or across the 180-degree line), so now is the last chance.
RULES, in order: 1) gameOver is true -> wait. 2) tapOutcome is 'pop' and waitOutcome is 'farther' or 'gameOver' -> tap. 3) tapOutcome is 'edge' and waitOutcome is 'gameOver' -> tap (last chance: waiting loses the dot). 4) Otherwise -> wait. Never tap when tapOutcome is 'miss', 'uncertain' or 'none'. pops counts the dots popped so far; unknown lists unrecognised objects, which are not threats.
